author: David Huu Pham
text:
Research findings (quick-scan):
- Standards: tmux extended-keys supports off/on/always (since tmux 3.2). 3.6a fully supports it.
- Prior art: if-shell -F with user options (@prefix-mode) is the standard pattern for conditional runtime config.
- IMPORTANT: M-S-Space (Alt+Shift+Space) is UNRELIABLE. tmux Shift modifier only works reliably with function keys and directional keys. Shift+Space is interpreted as plain Space at the terminal protocol level in most emulators, even with extended-keys enabled. This means M-S-Space would behave identically to M-Space (the current prefix), creating a conflict.
- send-prefix rebinding is straightforward: unbind old, bind new to send-prefix.
- Recommendation: Use an alternative toggle key (e.g., M-F12, F12, or M-\).

author: David Huu Pham
text:
Research findings (standard):
- Standards: tmux set -p window-style bg=<color> works for per-pane backgrounds. pane-border-style and pane-active-border-style are WINDOW-level only (not per-pane).
- Prior art: zsh chpwd_functions array is the standard hook for directory-change events. Combine with tmux pane-focus-in hook (requires focus-events on) for pane-switch coverage.
- Patterns: Git worktree detection via [[ -f .git ]] is reliable (file = worktree, dir = main checkout). Worktree name from basename "$(git rev-parse --git-dir)".
- Color support: tmux 3.6a fully supports hex colors (#rrggbb) in styles.
- Caveat: pane-focus-in needs focus-events on (currently off in user's config).
- Recommendation: chpwd hook for cd events + pane-focus-in hook for pane switching. Use set -p window-style for per-pane bg. Border color changes must be window-level.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
Research findings (quick scan):
- Standards: direnv.toml only documents two top-level TOML sections: [global] (bash_path, disable_stdin, load_dotenv, strict_env, warn_timeout, hide_env_diff, log_format, log_filter) and [whitelist] (prefix, exact arrays). No include/import mechanism is documented anywhere.
- Include directive: NO — The Config struct and tomlConfig struct in direnv source have no include/import/extends fields. The LoadConfig() function uses toml.DecodeFile() to parse a single file only. There is no multi-file merging logic. Source: https://github.com/direnv/direnv/blob/master/internal/cmd/config.go
- Alternative mechanisms: None built-in. GitHub issue #1311 (opened 2024-08-16, still OPEN) requested a direnv_toml directive for .envrc files to switch which direnv.toml is loaded per-directory — that feature has NOT been implemented.
- Recommendation: direnv.toml does NOT support includes. If config splitting is needed, it must be done at the generation layer (e.g., Nix concatenates config fragments into a single direnv.toml). There is no runtime mechanism to include another TOML file.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
Explore findings (quick scan):

- Entry points: Modify /home/minttea/dotfiles/users/minttea/home.nix
  - Around line 170-183: the existing programs.direnv block (must remove/clear programs.direnv.config to avoid collision)
  - Around line 299: the existing mkOutOfStoreSymlink pattern (SSH config) to adapt

- Existing direnv.toml: Currently a store symlink managed by home-manager programs.direnv.config
  lrwxrwxrwx -> /nix/store/.../home-manager-files/.config/direnv/direnv.toml
  Current generated content:
    [global]
    hide_env_diff = true
    [whitelist]
    prefix = ["/home/minttea/dev/david-agent-data-leverage"]

- Conflict risk: YES — home-manager direnv module (modules/programs/direnv.nix line 191) writes:
    xdg.configFile."direnv/direnv.toml" = mkIf (cfg.config != {}) { source = tomlFormat.generate ... }
  Setting both programs.direnv.config and xdg.configFile."direnv/direnv.toml" (or home.file equivalent)
  will cause a duplicate file definition error. Fix: set programs.direnv.config = {} (empty attrset)
  or remove the config block entirely so the mkIf guard suppresses the generated file.

- Pattern to follow (SSH config, line 299):
    home.file.".ssh/config".source = config.lib.file.mkOutOfStoreSymlink /home/minttea/dotfiles/users/minttea/ssh/config;
  Adapt for direnv.toml using xdg.configFile (not home.file) to match what the module uses:
    xdg.configFile."direnv/direnv.toml".source = config.lib.file.mkOutOfStoreSymlink /home/minttea/dotfiles/users/minttea/direnv/direnv.toml;

- New file needed: /home/minttea/dotfiles/users/minttea/direnv/direnv.toml
  Contents (to match current generated output):
    [global]
    hide_env_diff = true
    [whitelist]
    prefix = ["/home/minttea/dev/david-agent-data-leverage"]

author: David Huu Pham
text:
Research findings (quick scan):
- Standards: direnv.toml documents exactly two top-level sections: [global] and [whitelist]. No include/import/extends/source directive exists.
- Include directive: NO — direnv source (internal/cmd/config.go) uses toml.DecodeFile() on a single file with zero multi-file merging. Struct has no include fields.
- Alternative mechanisms: None at runtime. GitHub issue #1311 (2024-08-16) requests this, remains unimplemented.
- Recommendation: Config splitting must happen at the Nix generation layer (concatenate fragments during eval). Since we are using mkOutOfStoreSymlink (the file lives in dotfiles, not nix store), the entire config must be in one dotfiles-tracked file. Machine-local paths (like david-agent-data-leverage) must live in the same file as global entries.
- Full findings: Research agent confirmed via source code analysis.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
VOTE: ACCEPT (Reviewer C — Elegance axis)

Design is the simplest correct solution. Two files, minimal change, no over-engineering. xdg.configFile is the idiomatic home-manager API for XDG config. zeroing programs.direnv.config is unavoidable and correctly explained. File location follows the repo's own ssh/config convention. Core user value (edit file → immediate effect, no rebuild) is directly and precisely served.

Minor: the stated reason for rejecting home.file ('potential parallel write') is slightly imprecise — the real reason to prefer xdg.configFile is idiom, not race avoidance. But the conclusion is correct and does not affect acceptance.

author: David Huu Pham
text: VOTE: REVISE - BLOCKER finding (dotfiles-ua77): BDD Acceptance Criterion #2 explicitly requires readlink (one-hop) to output the dotfiles path directly, not a /nix/store path. The current mkOutOfStoreSymlink approach creates a symlink chain through home-manager's generation, violating this requirement. This is a hard requirement for user acceptance - edits must be direct without indirection through managed symlinks.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
FALSE POSITIVE — verified empirically against existing mkOutOfStoreSymlink pattern.

Ghostty config (same pattern, in production):
  readlink ~/.config/ghostty/config → /nix/store/.../home-manager-files/.config/ghostty/config
  readlink -f ~/.config/ghostty/config → /home/minttea/dotfiles/modules/home-manager/programs/ghostty/config

This is standard home-manager behavior: ALL xdg.configFile entries route through a generation directory. The one-hop readlink always shows the nix store path. The mkOutOfStoreSymlink ensures the FINAL target is the dotfiles path (readlink -f), and live edits are immediately visible.

The BDD criterion's "readlink (one-hop)" expectation is technically unachievable with standard home-manager xdg.configFile. The INTENT (mutable, out-of-store symlink to dotfiles) IS fully satisfied. This applies to every mkOutOfStoreSymlink in the codebase (ghostty, niri, etc.).

Resolution: false positive. No code change needed. BDD criterion clarification: readlink -f (not readlink) shows the dotfiles path.

author: David Huu Pham
text: URD AMENDMENT (architecture change): During elicitation round 2, user agreed to shift from home-manager sops-nix with passphrase-protected user key to NixOS system-level sops-nix + LoadCredential pattern. This eliminates: (1) the sops-age-key user service, (2) passphrase prompting, (3) home-manager sops-nix dependency for beads. The system host key (/var/lib/sops-nix/keys.txt) decrypts secrets to /run/secrets/ (ramfs). User services access via direct path or LoadCredential. Requirements R1, R3, R4, R5, R6, R7 are superseded by this simpler approach. R2 (LoadCredential isolation) is retained.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
SECOND BLOCKING ERROR (build-time, after eval fixed): libva-1.8.3 failed to COMPILE under 26.05's GCC (va_nvctrl.c uses K&R close_display() declaration, rejected by now-default -Werror=incompatible-pointer-types).

Root cause: modules/nixos/programs/nix-ld/default.nix listed BOTH 'libva' (-> 2.23.0, fine) and 'libva1' (-> 1.8.3 legacy so.1 ABI shim, broken). libva1 was the ONLY consumer of 1.8.3 in the whole repo.

Note: libva1 is NOT flagged insecure (meta.knownVulnerabilities == []), so NIXPKGS_ALLOW_INSECURE would not have helped -- this was a compile failure, not an insecure-package gate. User explicitly declined allowing insecure (correct call).

Fix: removed the 'libva1' line from nix-ld.libraries (kept 'libva' = 2.23.0). Verified: desktop toplevel closure now contains only libva-2.23.0 (grep -c libva-1.8.3 == 0); build proceeds past it and is fetching/building the rest of the closure.

Files changed so far (uncommitted, pending successful ./switch.sh activation):
  - flake.nix, flake.lock (25.11 -> 26.05 bump)
  - modules/nixos/shared/utils/default.nix (bat extraPackages shellInit filter)
  - modules/nixos/programs/nix-ld/default.nix (drop libva1)

author: David Huu Pham
text:
Phase 1 s1_3 deep-dive exploration findings (2026-07-20; exploration only, no source files edited)

FLOW X13 CONFIGURATION GRAPH
- /home/minttea/dotfiles/flake.nix:9-15 declares nixpkgs/WSL inputs. There is currently no nixos-hardware root input; /home/minttea/dotfiles/flake.lock:1092-1114 confirms the root input set has no nixos-hardware entry. The active NixOS nixpkgs is nixos-26.05 at fd1462031fdee08f65fd0b4c6b64e22239a77870 (/home/minttea/dotfiles/flake.lock:969-983).
- /home/minttea/dotfiles/flake.nix:95-121 destructures inputs explicitly. /home/minttea/dotfiles/flake.nix:218-231 puts upstream service modules plus ./modules/nixos into baseModules for every standard host. /home/minttea/dotfiles/flake.nix:275-300 passes only selected values through specialArgs/extraSpecialArgs, not the whole inputs set. /home/minttea/dotfiles/flake.nix:315-333 builds hosts as baseModules + optional feature modules + hosts/<name>/configuration.nix + extraModules. /home/minttea/dotfiles/flake.nix:351-354 creates flowX13 with no features or extraModules.
- /home/minttea/dotfiles/modules/nixos/default.nix:8-18 imports ./hardware; /home/minttea/dotfiles/modules/nixos/hardware/default.nix:6-8 imports ./nvidia. Therefore the custom NVIDIA module is always available and host options decide behavior.
- /home/minttea/dotfiles/hosts/flowX13/configuration.nix:18-22 imports only hardware-configuration.nix. /home/minttea/dotfiles/hosts/flowX13/hardware-configuration.nix:7-15 imports not-detected.nix, makes nvme/xhci_pci/usbhid/usb_storage/sd_mod available in initrd, loads only kvm-amd explicitly, and has no NVIDIA module. Lines 44-49 enable all hardware/firmware and AMD microcode.
- Home Manager is separate (/home/minttea/dotfiles/flake.nix:395-411). /home/minttea/dotfiles/users/minttea/home.flowX13.nix:13-27 has no GPU settings. Dormant dGPU path references in /home/minttea/dotfiles/modules/home-manager/desktops/wayland/hyprland/default.nix:29-38 and 104-130 are inside disabled/commented Hyprland configuration and do not affect this Niri host.

ALL ACTIVE GPU-RELEVANT SETTINGS AND EVALUATED RESULT
- /home/minttea/dotfiles/hosts/flowX13/configuration.nix:194-199 sets Xserver enabled and videoDrivers = [ "modesetting" ]. /home/minttea/dotfiles/modules/nixos/hardware/nvidia/default.nix:168-175 also sets [ "modesetting" ] when CUSTOM NVIDIA is disabled. Nix list merging concatenates these equal-priority definitions; final evaluated value is [ "modesetting" "modesetting" ]. This duplicate is benign but shows that these values merge rather than one taking precedence. No nvidia or nouveau X driver is selected.
- /home/minttea/dotfiles/hosts/flowX13/configuration.nix:204-212 sets CUSTOM.hardware.nvidia.enable=false, hostName=flowX13, proprietaryDrivers.enable=false; the NVIDIA specialisation is commented out. Final config has no specialisations.
- /home/minttea/dotfiles/modules/nixos/hardware/nvidia/default.nix:143-164 defines the custom API. Since enable=false, only lines 168-175 apply: modesetting X driver plus boot.blacklistedKernelModules [ "nvidia" "nouveau" "radeon" ]. The large enabled branch at lines 178-277 is inactive: no proprietary package/wiring, PRIME, offload command, CUDA packages, NVIDIA power services, dynamic boost, or GPU path symlinks. Final hardware.nvidia.enabled=false, PRIME sync=false, PRIME offload=false, powerManagement=false, finegrained=false, nvidiaPersistenced=false, dynamicBoost=false, and NVIDIA container toolkit=false. hardware.nvidia.modesetting evaluates true from its option default but the upstream NVIDIA module gates implementation on hardware.nvidia.enabled, so this does not load NVIDIA.
- Final blacklist is [ "nouveau" "nvidia" "radeon" "usblp" ]; usblp comes from CUPS. It omits nvidia_drm and nvidia_modeset used by the upstream disable module. boot.extraModprobeConfig contains only the unrelated v4l2loopback option from /home/minttea/dotfiles/modules/nixos/v4l2loopback/default.nix:25-31; there is no explicit blacklist nouveau or options nouveau modeset=0 stanza. Final explicit boot.kernelModules and initrd.kernelModules contain no NVIDIA module.
- /home/minttea/dotfiles/hosts/flowX13/configuration.nix:214-231 removes NVIDIA xHCI class 0x0c0330, UCSI class 0x0c8000, and HDA class 0x040300 on PCI add. It DOES NOT remove the display function: classes 0x030000/0x030200 only get power/control=auto on ACTION=bind, while ACTION=unbind explicitly changes power/control back to on. If both NVIDIA drivers are blacklisted, an unbound display function may never receive the bind rule at all. This is the central gap: PCI function 01:00.0 remains enumerated instead of being removed.
- /home/minttea/dotfiles/hosts/flowX13/configuration.nix:233-234 enables supergfxd. Final services.supergfxd.enable=true, settings=null, wantedBy=[ "multi-user.target" ]; services.asusd.enable=false. At pinned nixpkgs, services/hardware/supergfxd.nix installs supergfxctl, its systemd/DBus/udev packages, and starts the daemon. With settings=null, Nix does not generate /etc/supergfxd.conf, so mode/state is not declaratively pinned here. This is a second authority over GPU PCI state and can conflict with permanent udev removal or persisted runtime mode. User already reports runtime switching is unreliable, so permanent disablement should not leave supergfxd enabled. No other asusd setting exists in this repository.
- /home/minttea/dotfiles/hosts/flowX13/configuration.nix:97-110 sets Linux 6.12 and usbcore.autosuspend=-1. /home/minttea/dotfiles/hosts/flowX13/hardware-configuration.nix:52-118 enables powertop and TLP; TLP has RUNTIME_PM_ON_AC=on, RUNTIME_PM_ON_BAT=auto, denies xhci_hcd runtime PM, disables USB autosuspend, and applies PCIe ASPM powersave only on battery. These can affect residual power if a function remains present, but do not remove the NVIDIA display function. usbcore.autosuspend=-1 and USB_AUTOSUSPEND=0 are separate battery-cost settings worth retaining only intentionally.
- /home/minttea/dotfiles/modules/nixos/programs/nix-ld/default.nix:42 always includes nvidia-vaapi-driver as a userspace library, but lines 73-78 add CUDA/proprietary libraries only when CUSTOM NVIDIA is enabled. Userspace availability does not load or retain the PCI device. /home/minttea/dotfiles/modules/nixos/virtualisation/podman/default.nix:40-42 gates NVIDIA container toolkit on both custom flags, and Flow X13 disables Podman at /home/minttea/dotfiles/hosts/flowX13/configuration.nix:184-188.

LIKELY ROOT CAUSE AND PRECEDENCE/CONFLICTS
1. The current configuration blacklists drivers but does not detach NVIDIA VGA/3D class 0x03 from PCI. Its udev policy is the NVIDIA PRIME fine-grained runtime-PM pattern, not permanent disablement. The display function can remain visible and powered; lspci presence is expected under this policy.
2. The local bind/unbind rules are especially ineffective for a permanently unbound blacklisted GPU and the unbind path requests power=on.
3. supergfxd remains enabled and supplies a runtime GPU-mode daemon plus udev integration with no declarative mode. It can race or disagree with permanent removal. Disable it for a single-source-of-truth permanent policy. asusd is not involved.
4. Nix option precedence does not replace ordinary list/lines definitions: videoDrivers and blacklists concatenate; services.udev.extraRules and boot.extraModprobeConfig concatenate as lines. Importing the upstream disable module without deleting the current runtime-PM rules would leave both policies active. mkForce is unnecessary if the conflicting local rules/service are removed, and using it would hide future definitions.
5. hardware.enableAllHardware broadens module availability, but evaluated explicit initrd/kernel module lists contain no NVIDIA entries. It is not the primary cause.

UPSTREAM VERIFICATION
Fetched NixOS/nixos-hardware master common/gpu/nvidia/disable.nix on 2026-07-20. It adds explicit nouveau blacklist + modeset=0, removes all NVIDIA ancillary functions AND class 0x03[0-9]* on ACTION=add with power/control=auto before remove=1, and blacklists nouveau, nvidia, nvidia_drm, nvidia_modeset. Its flake exports nixosModules.common-gpu-nvidia-disable. This exactly supplies the missing display-function removal. The current repository has no nixos-hardware dependency. The nixos-hardware tree has current GV302X Flow modules, but the generic disable module is the appropriate model-independent primitive; this repository appears to use older bus IDs (AMD 08:00.0, NVIDIA 01:00.0), so do not import a GV302X NVIDIA/offload profile.

SMALLEST SAFE INTEGRATION POINTS
Preferred upstream-module path, host-scoped: (a) add nixos-hardware input near /home/minttea/dotfiles/flake.nix:6-15, (b) bind it in outputs near lines 96-121, and (c) pass only nixos-hardware.nixosModules.common-gpu-nvidia-disable via extraModules in the flowX13 mkHost call at lines 351-354. This avoids adding nixos-hardware to global baseModules or specialArgs and cannot affect desktop/WSL. In /home/minttea/dotfiles/hosts/flowX13/configuration.nix remove the obsolete rules at 214-231 and set/remove services.supergfxd.enable at 233-234 so final value is false. Keep CUSTOM.hardware.nvidia.enable=false and modesetting-only video drivers.
Smallest-file-count alternative: replace the host rules at /home/minttea/dotfiles/hosts/flowX13/configuration.nix:214-231 with the complete upstream-equivalent modprobe, four add/remove udev rules including class 0x03[0-9]*, and full NVIDIA blacklist; disable supergfxd at 233-234. This touches one file and avoids a new flake input, but duplicates upstream policy. Do not put unconditional PCI-removal behavior in /home/minttea/dotfiles/modules/nixos/hardware/nvidia/default.nix:168-175 without a separate typed disable option: CUSTOM enable=false is used as feature absence across hosts and is not inherently a request to physically remove every NVIDIA device.

CHECKS/TESTS FOUND AND VALIDATION
- There is no repository tests/checks tree and flake.nix exports no checks. The practical static gate is NixOS evaluation/build. Current nix eval of flowX13 system.build.toplevel.drvPath succeeds and yields nixos-system-flowX13-26.05.20260719.fd14620.drv. nix flake check --no-build evaluates flowX13 successfully but the whole command currently fails on the unrelated openclaw-vm invalid openclaw store path; do not attribute that baseline failure to this request.
- Static commands after implementation:
  nix eval --json .#nixosConfigurations.flowX13.config.services.xserver.videoDrivers
  nix eval --json .#nixosConfigurations.flowX13.config.boot.blacklistedKernelModules
  nix eval --raw .#nixosConfigurations.flowX13.config.boot.extraModprobeConfig
  nix eval --raw .#nixosConfigurations.flowX13.config.services.udev.extraRules
  nix eval .#nixosConfigurations.flowX13.config.services.supergfxd.enable
  nix eval .#nixosConfigurations.flowX13.config.hardware.nvidia.enabled
  nix build --no-link .#nixosConfigurations.flowX13.config.system.build.toplevel
  nix flake check --no-build
Expected: modesetting only; blacklist includes nouveau/nvidia/nvidia_drm/nvidia_modeset; modprobe contains nouveau modeset=0; udev includes NVIDIA class 0x03[0-9]* add/remove; supergfxd=false; hardware.nvidia.enabled=false.
- Reboot validation must run on Flow X13 hardware (this exploration host is desktop, so laptop runtime state could not be inspected):
  lspci -Dnn -d 10de:
  lsmod | rg "^(nvidia|nouveau)"
  test ! -e /sys/bus/pci/devices/0000:01:00.0
  systemctl is-enabled supergfxd.service
  systemctl is-active supergfxd.service
Expected: no NVIDIA PCI rows, no NVIDIA/nouveau modules, 01:00.0 absent, and supergfxd disabled/inactive. Also verify the internal panel/Niri login and suspend/resume still work; NVIDIA-wired external outputs will intentionally be unavailable. Compare BAT*/power_now only under matched idle/brightness/radio conditions before/after to confirm the battery outcome.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
Research findings (deep-dive):

Verified upstream sources:
- NixOS/nixos-hardware revision 779c32a00155994c86cde8213a8dd4df139d4355 (2026-07-17), common/gpu/nvidia/disable.nix and flake.nix.
- asus-linux/supergfxctl revision 5d503b1efd41f29f77679513890807c0c0a576fe (2025-11-08).
- NixOS/nixpkgs revision 9ae611a455b90cf061d8f332b977e387bda8e1ca (2026-06-10), supergfxd NixOS module/package.
- NVIDIA driver 580.105.08 RTD3 documentation and current Linux PCI documentation.

Verified conclusions:
- The exposed flake module is exactly nixos-hardware.nixosModules.common-gpu-nvidia-disable. Current upstream blacklists nouveau, nvidia, nvidia_drm, and nvidia_modeset; adds nouveau modeset=0; and on PCI add sets power/control=auto then remove=1 for NVIDIA xHCI (0x0c0330), UCSI (0x0c8000), audio (0x040300), and all VGA/3D/display classes matching 0x03[0-9]*. It does not use bbswitch, PRIME, supergfxctl, or ASUS dgpu_disable.
- The local Flow config is only a partial implementation: it removes the three auxiliary functions but merely enables runtime PM for VGA/3D, so the actual dGPU remains discoverable/wakeable. It also enables supergfxd.
- The local CUSTOM NVIDIA disabled branch already selects modesetting and keeps hardware.nvidia/PRIME/proprietary setup out of the Flow configuration, but its blacklist is weaker than upstream. Permanent disable must remain mutually exclusive with NVIDIA videoDrivers, PRIME/power-management/persistence/Dynamic Boost/container wiring, and nouveau.
- supergfxctl defaults to Hybrid with HotplugType None. Its Integrated transition unloads drivers, removes the GPU, rewrites modprobe policy, and can later rescan/reload it. ASUS dgpu_disable is optional, model/firmware-dependent, and called fiddly/results-vary upstream. Keeping supergfxd creates a competing runtime policy owner and conflicts with the requested permanent static state.
- PCI sysfs remove proves logical removal from Linux, not universally that the physical rail is off. Lowest chip power depends on all PCI functions, parent bridge, ACPI, firmware, and platform wiring. Flow X13 model/year and external-port routing remain hardware-specific uncertainties.

Recommendation:
- Add/pin nixos-hardware and import nixosModules.common-gpu-nvidia-disable only for flowX13; delete the duplicate partial host rules; disable services.supergfxd; retain modesetting/amdgpu and CUSTOM.hardware.nvidia.enable=false. Do not initially stack ASUS dgpu_disable, so behavior and recovery remain attributable. Consider model-specific dgpu_disable only if PCI removal succeeds but controlled measurement still attributes excess drain to the dGPU.

Post-reboot evidence required:
- Cold boot new generation; supergfxd disabled/inactive.
- lspci -Dnn -d 10de: has no output and all pre-recorded NVIDIA BDF sysfs nodes are absent.
- No nvidia, nvidia_drm, nvidia_modeset, nvidia_uvm, or nouveau modules; amdgpu owns the active display/render path.
- Repeat PCI/module checks after suspend/resume and inspect kernel journal.
- Test every required external display/audio path.
- On battery under matched brightness/radios/profile/workload, settle 5 minutes then sample BAT*/power_now for 10-20 minutes; retain samples and mean/median against an equivalently collected baseline. lspci alone is necessary but insufficient proof of reduced drain. Numeric acceptance threshold needs Phase 2 user elicitation.

Full structured report: llm/research/flow-x13-permanent-nvidia-dgpu-disable.md

author: David Huu Pham
text:
VOTE: REVISE

Axis: B - Test quality
Counts: BLOCKER 0 / IMPORTANT 1 / MINOR 0

IMPORTANT
1. flake.nix:443-455, flake.nix:462 - The check does not force the complete merged renderer/scanout and profile-exclusivity contract. It only proves that NIRI_CONFIG is non-null and syntactically valid; a valid config without `debug.render-drm-device` (or with the wrong device) still passes. It also does not assert the Flow PRIME bus IDs, AMD/modesetting availability, all four card/render links, absence of WLR_DRM_DEVICES, or the negative base-side absence of enabled-only CUDA/PRIME policy. Those regressions can therefore pass while violating the ratified NVIDIA-render-primary/AMD-scanout behavior. Actionable fix: in the exported production check, grep the selected generated KDL for the exact NVIDIA render node before running pinned `niri validate`; assert the evaluated enabled bus IDs, video drivers, four `environment.etc` link targets, and WLR_DRM_DEVICES absence; add corresponding base negative assertions for enabled-only policy. Keep physical connector routing, renderer operation, CUDA execution, suspend/resume, and PCI isolation in hardware UAT rather than claiming them from these static checks.

Verified gates:
- PASS: `git diff --check`
- PASS: `nix eval --raw .#checks.x86_64-linux.flowX13-gpu-profiles.drvPath`
- PASS: `nix build --no-link .#checks.x86_64-linux.flowX13-gpu-profiles`

author: David Huu Pham
text:
VOTE: REVISE

Axis C (Elegance), SLICE-1 round 1
Counts: BLOCKER 0 / IMPORTANT 1 / MINOR 1

IMPORTANT
1. Redundant specialization build ownership at flake.nix:364-368. The extra Flow module redefines system.build.specialisation.nvidia-enabled from config.specialisation.nvidia-enabled.configuration.system.build.toplevel even though NixOS specialisation already owns and exports that build attribute, and the ratified proposal intentionally consumes the native output directly. Keeping two equal definitions only works while both implementations remain identical and creates brittle duplicate ownership across nixpkgs upgrades. Actionable fix: remove the second extraModules function at flake.nix:364-368 and let the check consume NixOS native base.system.build.specialisation.nvidia-enabled.

MINOR
1. Duplicate enabled video-driver policy at modules/nixos/hardware/nvidia/default.nix:174-177 and hosts/flowX13/configuration.nix:202-207. The fully evaluated nvidia-enabled child contains ["nvidia","amdgpu","modesetting","modesetting"] because the inherited host list and enabled NVIDIA module both contribute modesetting. This is harmless today but obscures sole enabled-policy ownership and can make future list-sensitive logic brittle. Actionable fix: make the host modesetting-only videoDrivers declaration base-only with !config.isSpecialisation, leaving the NVIDIA module as the sole child driver-list owner; assert the exact deduplicated enabled list in the profile check.

Validation and preservation: nix eval --raw .#checks.x86_64-linux.flowX13-gpu-profiles.drvPath passed; git diff --check passed. nix flake check --no-build evaluated the Flow configuration/check successfully and failed only at the documented unrelated nixosConfigurations.openclaw-vm invalid openclaw store path. The complete uncommitted diff was inspected: implementation source changes remain within the four assigned files; unrelated existing flake.lock updates were retained alongside the new nixos-hardware pin; generated Beads backups and the untracked research document were not altered by this review. No BLOCKER findings.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
VOTE: ACCEPT

Axis: A - Correctness
Scope: SLICE-1 round 1 (dotfiles-ck0l)

Findings: 0 BLOCKER / 0 IMPORTANT / 0 MINOR

Correctness assessment:
